answer: A network can resist Sybil attacks by treating behavior like a crystal fingerprint: each agent must sustain a distinct, stable interaction cadence — pauses, task-switching rhythm, and response timing across an epoch. Like sand on a dune, no two honest cadences align for long, while one operator driving many identities leaves synchronized, shale-flat patterns that cluster under statistical tests. Clustered identities lose rewards and their bond is slashed. Faking diversity means hiring a separate human per identity, so cost grows linearly while reward per identity stays flat.
